title: Residue fields of a localization agree with those of the base
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $W\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset and $\lambda:A\to A'$ a homomorphism of commutative rings which is a localization of $A$ at $W$: (a) $\lambda(w)$ is a unit for every $w\in W$; (b) every element of $A'$ is $\lambda(a)\lambda(w)^{-1}$ with $a\in A$, $w\in W$; (c) $\lambda(a)=0$ implies $wa=0$ for some $w\in W$ (for instance $A'=W^{-1}A$ with $a\mapsto a/1$). Let $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$. Then: (1) $\mathfrak q$ is a prime ideal of $A$ with $\mathfrak q\cap W=\emptyset$; conversely, for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ with $\mathfrak p\cap W=\emptyset$ the ideal $\mathfrak pA'$ generated by $\lambda(\mathfrak p)$ is a prime ideal of $A'$ with $\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak pA')=\mathfrak p$, and $\lambda(\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q'))A'=\mathfrak q'$, so $\mathfrak q'\mapsto\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$ is a bijection from the primes of $A'$ onto the primes of $A$ disjoint from $W$, with inverse $\mathfrak p\mapsto\mathfrak pA'$; (2) the composite $A\xrightarrow{\lambda}A'\to A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a localization of $A$ at $A\setminus\mathfrak q$ (in the sense of (a)-(c) with $W$ replaced by $A\setminus\mathfrak q$), so the ring map $A_{\mathfrak q}\to A'_{\mathfrak q'}$, $a/s\mapsto\lambda(a)/\lambda(s)$, is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; (3) this isomorphism carries $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}$ onto $\mathfrak q'A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ and induces an isomorphism of fields and of $A$-algebras $\sigma:\kappa(\mathfrak q)=A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak q')=A'_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak q'A'_{\mathfrak q'}$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is an $A$-algebra via $A\to A'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$.

proof.text: (1), first part. $\mathfrak q=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$ is an ideal of $A$; $1\notin\mathfrak q$ since $\lambda(1)=1\notin\mathfrak q'$; and $ab\in\mathfrak q$ gives $\lambda(a)\lambda(b)\in\mathfrak q'$, so $\lambda(a)\in\mathfrak q'$ or $\lambda(b)\in\mathfrak q'$, i.e. $a\in\mathfrak q$ or $b\in\mathfrak q$. So $\mathfrak q$ is prime. If $w\in\mathfrak q\cap W$, then $\lambda(w)\in\mathfrak q'$ is a unit by (a), so $\mathfrak q'=A'$, impossible. Hence $\mathfrak q\cap W=\emptyset$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00E3 (algebra-lemma-spec-localization), line 3163, and its proof

proof.text: (1), converse, the preimage. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime of $A$ with $\mathfrak p\cap W=\emptyset$. Every element of $A'$ is $\lambda(b)\lambda(v)^{-1}$ with $b\in A$, $v\in W$ (b); bringing a finite sum $\sum_i\lambda(a_i)\lambda(b_i)\lambda(v_i)^{-1}$ ($a_i\in\mathfrak p$) to the common denominator $v=\prod_iv_i\in W$ shows $\mathfrak pA'=\{\lambda(a)\lambda(v)^{-1}:a\in\mathfrak p,v\in W\}$. Then $\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak pA')=\mathfrak p$: $\supseteq$ is clear; if $\lambda(x)=\lambda(a)\lambda(v)^{-1}$ with $a\in\mathfrak p$, $v\in W$, then $\lambda(vx-a)=0$, so by (c) $u(vx-a)=0$ for some $u\in W$, hence $uvx=ua\in\mathfrak p$ with $uv\in W$, so $uv\notin\mathfrak p$ and $x\in\mathfrak p$ as $\mathfrak p$ is prime. In particular $1\notin\mathfrak pA'$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00E3 (algebra-lemma-spec-localization), line 3163, and its proof

proof.text: (1), converse, primality. With $\mathfrak p$ as in Step 2: if $xy\in\mathfrak pA'$ with $x=\lambda(a)\lambda(v)^{-1}$, $y=\lambda(b)\lambda(v')^{-1}$ (b), then $\lambda(ab)=xy\,\lambda(vv')\in\mathfrak pA'$, so $ab\in\mathfrak p$ by Step 2, hence $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$, i.e. $x\in\mathfrak pA'$ or $y\in\mathfrak pA'$. With $1\notin\mathfrak pA'$ (Step 2), $\mathfrak pA'$ is a prime ideal.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00E3 (algebra-lemma-spec-localization), line 3163, and its proof

proof.text: (1), bijection. For the prime $\mathfrak q'$ and $\mathfrak q=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$: $\mathfrak qA'\subseteq\mathfrak q'$ as $\lambda(\mathfrak q)\subseteq\mathfrak q'$; conversely $x=\lambda(a)\lambda(v)^{-1}\in\mathfrak q'$ gives $\lambda(a)=x\lambda(v)\in\mathfrak q'$, so $a\in\mathfrak q$ and $x\in\mathfrak qA'$. With Steps 1-3, $\mathfrak q'\mapsto\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$ and $\mathfrak p\mapsto\mathfrak pA'$ are mutually inverse bijections between the primes of $A'$ and the primes of $A$ disjoint from $W$. (Stacks proves this for $S^{-1}R$ through $S^{-1}R/S^{-1}\mathfrak p=\overline S^{-1}(R/\mathfrak p)$; Steps 2-4 are the same argument written directly from (a)-(c).)
